Hi Kimberly!

Thanks for your message. I think that TK was somewhat, though not greatly,
successful in bringing certain issues to the attention of the general public -
issues that were brewing in the back of many people's minds, and that the mass
media (bought and paid for by the corporate kings) would never touch. Issues
that other people have written about too.

That was step one. Step two, imo, requires serious critical discussion, and
that is up to everyone who has heard anything of this message.

But, if TK mainly succeded in inspiring thoughtless fanatics, then he was a
dismal failure.

Due to mass publishing, his plan to smash technology will not work any more
than plans of the religious groups who burned Beatles albums in the '60s.

Happily, there are newsgroups such as this. And happily, there are more
activists groups out there these days that are working within legal and
non-violent means to promote change.

I am somewhat curious about something. In paragraph 15, TK writes, "Leftists
tend to hate anything that has an image of being strong, good and successful...
He hates America and the West because they are strong and successful." So, if
the West and its civilization is so *good*, or strong and successful, what is
the problem with making changes via reform? (And I hope that anyone who may
answer this will not quote the anti-reform part of the  manifesto without an
argument of their own!)

I figure that reform has a better chance than anarchy.

-Susan
